USMLE-style practice · Pediatrics

First wheezing illness in infancy

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 5-month-old has two days of rhinorrhea followed by cough, tachypnea and reduced feeding. Examination shows diffuse crackles, wheeze and mild recession. This is the first such episode. Which diagnosis best fits?

  1. Acute viral bronchiolitis
  2. Foreign body aspiration
  3. Typical lobar bacterial pneumonia
  4. Acute epiglottitis
  5. Established allergic asthma
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Acute viral bronchiolitis

The coryzal prodrome followed by diffuse small-airway findings in an infant is characteristic.

Understanding the options

Acute viral bronchiolitis
The coryzal prodrome followed by diffuse small-airway findings in an infant is characteristic.
Foreign body aspiration
Aspiration usually begins abruptly and may cause focal or asymmetric findings.
Typical lobar bacterial pneumonia
Lobar pneumonia more often produces focal findings and higher fever.
Acute epiglottitis
Epiglottitis presents with upper-airway symptoms such as drooling and painful swallowing.
Established allergic asthma
A first wheezing episode at this age without recurrent symptoms is more consistent with bronchiolitis.
